Subject: Fast turnaround, careful machining, and they actually read the drawing

We used Arroyo Precision Works for two parts for our near-infrared camera: a camera-to-dewar adapter plate and a light baffle tube, both 6061-T6 and black anodized. The parts were needed for a telescope run at Palomar, so the schedule mattered a lot.

Turnaround was the biggest surprise. The purchase order quoted 21 days. The parts were back and at our loading dock in 9 days, anodizing included. A large vendor had quoted us about six weeks for similar work, so we went with Arroyo, and I'm glad we did.

What made the difference for me was that they actually read the drawing. During setup, Tiff at Arroyo noticed that the bolt circle on sheet 2 was written as 4.125 mm, while every other dimension on the drawing was in millimeters. The mistake was mine. I had copied that dimension from an old drawing for a previous camera. Ruben emailed to check before they cut anything, and that check saved us from a plate where the screws would have landed inside the bore. I would much rather a shop ask a question than machine the wrong part exactly as drawn. Any lab that sends drawings to a shop should know that this kind of care is what you're paying for.

Our fit test on November 9 went very well. All eight screws seated on the dewar with no forcing. Flatness across the plate face measured under 0.01 mm on the dial indicator. The baffle threads ran smoothly, and a dark test with the lab lights on and a 300 second dark frame matched the closed dewar, so there was no light leak. The anodizing was even with no bare spots.

Ruben also drove the parts over to Robinson Lab himself on his way to another job, and there was no delivery charge. Small things like that make it easy to work with a shop again.

For prototype and short-run parts where the drawing matters and the schedule is real, I'd recommend Arroyo without hesitation. The quality is consistent, communication was fast and clear whenever a decision was needed, and they delivered well ahead of their own estimate. I'd also ask purchasing to consider adding them to the preferred vendor list.

Rating: 5/5
